criterion.summary: p_astro > 0.5 (worded 'greater than 0.5', '> 0.5' and 'at least one half' in different places), following GWTC-2.1 and 3-OGC. Hanford-Livingston coincident BBH search only. p_astro is the declaration statistic; IFAR is per bank and not used for declaration.
criterion.quote: In this work we report ten new BBH merger events, declarable under the criteria that the signal's probability of astrophysical origin, $\pastro$, is at least one half (following \citet{lvc_o3a_deep_gwtc2_1_update_2021} and \citet{nitz_o3a_3ogc_catalog_2021}).
criterion.section: Sec. I Introduction. Also: Abstract ('compile a catalog of signals that pass a significance threshold of astrophysical probability greater than 0.5 (following the GWTC-2.1 and 3-OGC catalogs)'); Sec. IV ('The astrophysical probability is the statistic used to determine whether a signal is declared as a detection, whereas the false alarm rate tells us how often the detector noise produces a trigger of a given SNR peaking in the same frequency band as that template'); Sec. V.B Concluding remarks ('declared based on the criteria that $\pastro > 0.5$'); Table I caption 'New events with $p_{\rm astro} > 0.5$'.

tiers.name: new events (10)
tiers.quote: We report the detection of ten new binary black hole (BBH) mergers in the publicly released data from the the first half of the third observing run (O3a)
tiers.section: Abstract; Table I (tab:signalsFound); Sec. III 'Newly Reported BBH mergers'

tiers.name: previously reported GWTC-2.1 HL events re-detected (31)
tiers.quote: We confirm the significance of all but six of the 37 Hanford--Livingston coincident BBH mergers reported by \citet{lvc_o3a_deep_gwtc2_1_update_2021}, with three LVC candidates vetoed by our pipeline (failing signal consistency or excess power tests), and three LVC candidates falling below the detection threshold (see Table~\ref{tab:lvc events}).
tiers.section: Sec. I; Table II; Sec. IV 'Comparison to previously reported catalogues'

tiers.name: revoked GWTC-2 event recovered (1: GW190909_114149)
tiers.quote: We also detect GW190909\_114149, which was reduced to sub-threshold between GWTC-2 \cite{lvc_o3a_gwtc2_catalog_2021} and GWTC-2.1 \cite{lvc_o3a_deep_gwtc2_1_update_2021}, and this puts the total at 42 BBH mergers detected in our pipeline's Hanford--Livingston coincident search of the O3a data

below_criterion.notes: All are GWTC-2.1 events in Table II: 3 vetoed by IAS (p_astro '---', IFAR 'Veto') and 3 with p_astro < 0.5. The paper coins no GW-style names for sub-threshold IAS candidates. The text also names (untabulated) LVC marginal candidates GW190531_023648 and GW190426_152155 as sub-threshold in IAS too. The vetoed GW190521_030229 is called 'GW190521' in the text.

open_questions: Designation inconsistency: Table II row 'GW190917_114629' (p_astro 0.35, below threshold) is written 'GW190917_114630' in the Sec. IV and Sec. V text.
p_astro discrepancies between Table I and captions/text: GW190821_124821 (table 0.60, caption/text 0.61) and GW190920_113516 (table 0.57, caption/text 0.58). The table value is used as p_astro.
Criterion wording varies ('greater than 0.5', '> 0.5', 'at least one half'); no event sits at exactly 0.5, so it makes no difference here.

Short form 'GW190814' in this paper means the LVK LV-coincident event (excluded from the search), not the new IAS event GW190814_192009; 'GW190521' means the vetoed GW190521_030229. A matcher must not resolve GW190814 to GW190814_192009.

Sec. IV 'Marginally recovered candidates' lists GW190426_190642 as below threshold, then says 'GW190426_152155 was unfortunately not covered by our banks'; probably a typo for GW190426_190642 (cf. Sec. II). Not a detection either way.
